Below 50 it costs more than it builds. 40 to 60 is the median range, where the reading crosses the line in both directions. The solar plexus, behind your stomach, is the most complex bundle of nerves outside the brain that runs without you thinking about it. Power, self-worth, shame and will are all stored here, because this is where the body works out where it stands with the world. The gut feeling of "can I handle this?" comes from here. About a third of every pattern in the catalog sits at this seat. Every big saboteur group in the catalog has its root address here.

The nerves around the heart take in branches of the vagus nerve, which carry news about other people up from the gut. Grief, love, being left and forgiving are stored here, because the heart carries what happens between you and other people through its nerves. About 15 in every 100 patterns released here have had their opposite installed, second only to the root. When heart patterns clear, their opposites install well.

The nerves in your neck run the parts you speak with. Holding your voice back is a charge in those nerves, a real tightening around your throat and mouth, laid down every time you were shut up, shamed for speaking or punished for having a voice. Voice suppression alone is 405 patterns, far more than anything else at the throat. It is not about confidence. It is the nerves at the top of your neck firing the moment you go to speak.

The trigeminal nerve is the biggest nerve in the head, and it links into the nerves you see with. Being stuck on a choice, or not knowing which way to go, is not a thinking problem. It is a charge in those nerves that fires just as you are about to pick a direction. Vision and direction carry 123 patterns, more than anything else here. The charge that stops you seeing your next step has an exact address in a nerve of the head.

Every sentence that starts with I am is stored at the crown, because this is where all the nerves of the head meet. Every belief about who you are, and every story that keeps you small, runs through the pineal gland and a net of nerves in the brainstem. The crown is not a spiritual place. It is a meeting point of nerves. There are 196 identity patterns here, each one an I am sentence that keeps you small, fired by the nerves like a command.

Survival charge is stored here, in the nerves at the base of the spine, because the body's first question, am I safe?, runs through its lowest nerves. Not having enough, getting hurt and being pushed out of the group all land here. Of the patterns released here, about 28 in every 100 have had their opposite installed, the most of any seat. This layer is on the move.

Making things and wanting things are stored here, in the nerves of the lower belly and pelvis, because these are the body's making nerves. Holding back what you want to make is a charge here, and these nerves fire every time you stop yourself. Only about 3 in every 100 patterns released here have had their opposite installed, the fewest of any seat. The charge from holding back runs deeper here than anywhere else.

The solar plexus, behind your stomach, is the most complex bundle of nerves outside the brain that runs without you thinking about it. Power, self-worth, shame and will are all stored here, because this is where the body works out where it stands with the world. The gut feeling of "can I handle this?" comes from here. About a third of every pattern in the catalog sits at this seat. Every big saboteur group in the catalog has its root address here.

The nerves around the heart take in branches of the vagus nerve, which carry news about other people up from the gut. Grief, love, being left and forgiving are stored here, because the heart carries what happens between you and other people through its nerves. About 15 in every 100 patterns released here have had their opposite installed, second only to the root. When heart patterns clear, their opposites install well.

The nerves in your neck run the parts you speak with. Holding your voice back is a charge in those nerves, a real tightening around your throat and mouth, laid down every time you were shut up, shamed for speaking or punished for having a voice. Voice suppression alone is 405 patterns, far more than anything else at the throat. It is not about confidence. It is the nerves at the top of your neck firing the moment you go to speak.
Optic / Trigeminal / Cranial Nerves (CN II, V)

The trigeminal nerve is the biggest nerve in the head, and it links into the nerves you see with. Being stuck on a choice, or not knowing which way to go, is not a thinking problem. It is a charge in those nerves that fires just as you are about to pick a direction. Vision and direction carry 123 patterns, more than anything else here. The charge that stops you seeing your next step has an exact address in a nerve of the head.

Every sentence that starts with I am is stored at the crown, because this is where all the nerves of the head meet. Every belief about who you are, and every story that keeps you small, runs through the pineal gland and a net of nerves in the brainstem. The crown is not a spiritual place. It is a meeting point of nerves. There are 196 identity patterns here, each one an I am sentence that keeps you small, fired by the nerves like a command.

Argues against your own intentions. Always sounds reasonable. Never says stop forever, says stop today. The fear of discomfort is mild enough to be rationalized away. The happiness available from the easier option is just high enough to make the rationalization feel earned. Together they produce the internal diplomat who can talk you out of anything, not through force, but through the perfectly reasonable argument that now is not the right moment. The most dangerous saboteur in the system because it sounds exactly like you.
The moment between intending to do the necessary thing and beginning to do it. The pause.
Begin the action before the internal dialogue completes. Remove the pause. The Negotiator only has power in the gap between intention and motion. Close the gap.
I can start tomorrow. / Just this once. / I've earned a break.

Hypervigilance at the level of outcomes. The foundation of the Type A pattern. Not a personality trait, a fear response that has been running so long it looks like a management style. The fear underneath: something will go wrong, someone will get hurt, or the situation will fall apart if I release my grip. Self-control registers as 10. Anything less registers as loss. The delta between perceived control and actual control is the zone of active saboteur behavior. Anger layers in as a do-as-I-say mechanism, authority used to close the control gap quickly. Entitlement provides the justification: it is not just that I need to control this. It is that I am right to. Competition drives the adversarial edge, not just winning but not-losing, which is a different frequency entirely.
The moment control begins to slip. Uncertainty in outcomes. Others not performing to expectation. Delegation without confirmation. Silence where confirmation should be.

Control is a belief held under pressure. The person fails control the same way a person fails a landing, only if they quit. Recognize that the need to be in control and the experience of being out of control are both charges, not conditions. Neither is real. Locate the fear underneath. Release the fear. The need to control loses what it was standing on.
If I don't control this, something will go wrong.
Focuses on internal feelings and victim mentality for attention. Martyrdom.
Identify one thing within your control. Take one action on it.
Continuous pressure to do better. Anxiety about imperfections in self and others.
Before completion or release of work.
Set a fixed completion time. Release at that time regardless of state.
It is not good enough yet.
Indirectly tries to gain acceptance by helping, pleasing, rescuing, or flattering.
When there is potential for disapproval or when a boundary is needed.
State a preference or limit once. Do not explain or apologize.
My worth depends on making others happy.
Dependent on constant performance for self-respect. Workaholic.
When performance is not being measured or when rest is available.
Rest without producing for one hour. No metrics.
My worth is in my output.
Processes everything through logic. Impatient with emotional concerns.
Name the emotion present in the room before analyzing the problem.
If I can't explain it, it isn't real.
Continuous anxiety about potential dangers. Constant risk management.
When the environment changes or trust is required.
Identify one thing that is safe. Hold that for 60 seconds.
The threat is always just ahead.
Constant search for new activities. Rarely at peace with the current moment.
When the current situation becomes familiar or stable.
Stay with the current thing for twice as long as the impulse to move suggests.
The next thing will be better.
Perfectionism and need for order. Anxiety when standards are not met.
When the environment or person deviates from the correct way.
Identify one situation where your standard is serving your fear, not your values.
There is a right way and a wrong way.
Judges self and others. Replays past failures. The master saboteur, activates all others.
When someone, including self, falls short of standard.
Find one thing that is right about the situation being judged.
Does not own. Justification to avoid accountability.
When direct accountability or personal disclosure is required.
Stay with the direct question for 10 seconds before redirecting.
If they knew the real me they would leave.
Amplifies the emotional intensity of situations to generate attention or movement.
When intensity of feeling is present and an audience is available.
Reduce the intensity of the next statement by half.
My pain must be visible to matter.
Runs continuous worst-case scenarios. Mistakes anxiety for planning.
Name the specific worst case. Name one action if it occurs.

Withdraws from contact as protection. Independence as defense, not a value. Fear of rejection co-mingling with shame of belonging at sufficient magnitude. The person does not experience themselves as afraid, they experience themselves as preferring solitude. Release the fear and sad nodes and the solitude remains if chosen, not if driven.
When connection is available and would be beneficial.
Make one direct request for connection.
Approval-seeking at the expense of authenticity.
When approval is uncertain or a boundary is needed.
Identify the response that serves the relationship rather than the approval.
If they don't like me I have failed.
Defaults to distrust and doubt. Skepticism as protection against disappointment.
When new information challenges the current model.
Sit with the new information for 24 hours before dismissing it.
Lives in possibility without building the bridge toward it. Avoids the friction of execution.
When the gap between vision and current reality is visible.
Identify one concrete step. Execute it today.
Someday the conditions will be right.
Delays action on important tasks. Mistakes motion for progress.
When the important task is clear and available.
Begin. Not finish. Not plan. Begin. Three minutes.
Believes their competence is unearned and discoverable as fraud.
When competence is being evaluated or recognition is offered.
Identify one thing you know that the room does not. State it.
They will find out I do not belong here.
Uses anger and force to override resistance. Mistakes compliance for agreement.
When authority is challenged or outcome is not proceeding as required.
Pause 5 seconds. Name the fear underneath the anger before responding.
Sacrifices for others to generate obligation or moral authority.
When sacrifice has been made and goes unrecognized.
Identify whether the sacrifice was chosen or performed. If performed, stop.
I give everything and receive nothing.
When hope or enthusiasm is present in self or others.
Identify one thing good about the situation being dismissed.
Achieves outcomes indirectly through influence, withholding, or positioning.
When the direct approach feels risky.
State the actual need directly. Once. Without positioning.
Loops on decisions past the point of useful analysis.
When a decision is required and the outcome is uncertain.
Set a decision time limit. Decide at that limit. Do not extend it.
More analysis will produce the right answer.
Uses pleasure, distraction, or movement to exit discomfort before it resolves.
When the present moment is uncomfortable and an exit is available.
Stay in the discomfort for two minutes. Name what is present.
I just need to not feel this right now.
Declines the engagement before it can cost anything. Not fleeing discomfort the way the Escapist does, and not arguing the way the Negotiator does. Not present for it.
When something asks to be dealt with and not dealing with it carries no immediate penalty.
Name the thing being avoided out loud, then do the smallest piece of it.
If I stay unaware, nothing can land on me.
Removes the foundation of meaning as a pre-emptive strike against disappointment.
When meaning is required to justify effort.
Identify one action worth doing regardless of meaning. Do it.
Nothing matters enough to sustain effort.
Maintains deliberate unawareness to avoid responsibility or conflict.
When complexity, conflict, or moral weight is present.
Name one thing you know that you are pretending not to know.
I don't want to be involved.
Pre-empts positive outcomes by building a case against them before they materialize.
When a positive outcome is possible.
Name the best thing that could really happen. Act from that.
Pictures the worst outcome in every unknown. The Worrywart does this on a smaller scale. The Catastrophizer jumps from an ordinary unknown to a threat to survival.
Describe the actual current situation without projection. Stay in the present tense.
Backs up the harmful patterns of others to keep the relationship or avoid conflict. Not the same as the Pleaser: the Enabler backs up behavior they know is harmful.
When someone they care about is repeating a destructive pattern.
Name what you see. Once. Without attachment to the response.
If I say something they will leave.

The colloquial name for the Controller and Hyper-Vigilant composite at Type A intensity. Hypervigilance running on outcomes and on threat at the same time. The body is scanning forward (what could go wrong) and downward (am I in command of this) in continuous loop. Reads to other people as competence under pressure. Reads in the body as never landing. The same fear that drives Controller (something will go wrong if I release grip) and the same fear that drives Hyper-Vigilant (the threat is just ahead) co-mingle here at sufficient magnitude that they cannot be felt as separate. Distinct from Controller alone: Control Freak does not wait for the control gap to open before acting. Distinct from Hyper-Vigilant alone: Control Freak organizes the scan around its own agency, not around external monitoring. Type A is the social presentation. The somatic state is sustained sympathetic activation that the body has normalized as baseline.
Any environment the person did not configure. Any outcome the person did not design. Any silence where confirmation should be.

Lock the jaw, the shoulders, and the diaphragm for a count of five. Notice they were already locked. Release on the exhale. The drill shows the body can hold a state without scanning it. Repeat until the scan stops without being asked to.
If I am not running this, no one is.

pattern recognition, codification, teaching, symbolic thinking. The person who reads before being asked to. Somatic knowledge is true knowledge, once it's in the body, deception doesn't work on you. You can feel the lie before it forms a word.
over-intellectualization, false certainty, knowledge as a barrier rather than a bridge.
bridging, translation, exact words, quick thinking. The connector, the person who translates between people, between ideas, between worlds.
manipulation, saying one thing and then another, using what you know to get a hold over people.
physical courage, holding your ground, guarding what matters. Force aimed at what is in the way, not at people.
domination, violence without purpose, war as identity.
governance, structural authority, organizing chaos into function. sees how systems should be organized.

building, executing, bringing vision into form. Always needed to make things. When you can't create it feels like disconnection, like the system is broken. Financial stress kills creativity not motivationally but anatomically: the survival charge consumes the current before it reaches the generative center. When the root clears, the sacral opens, the creative current flows again. Not as discipline. As a natural consequence of the channel being clear.
perfectionism as paralysis, identity tied to output.
deliberate dissolution, clearing what's false or finished, making space for what comes next. Sees what needs to end.
destruction as identity, nihilism, chaos without rebuilding.
union, intimacy, the force that draws beings into genuine contact. Love as a state the person generates, not receives. Always knew what brings people together.
codependency, possession, love as completion rather than addition.
directed intervention, active clearing, creating conditions in which restoration happens. Finds the broken thing in any room.
rescuer complex, martyrdom, healing as identity.

voluntary descent, the chosen ordeal, sacrifice as the mechanism that produces insight unavailable any other way. The knowledge that comes from what was given up, not accumulated. The real use of experience: take in as much as you can, then let go of the names you gave it. Words illuminate, they don't contain.
suffering as identity, the descent without return.

discernment of what's real and what's false. Accountability without cruelty. Moral disorder doesn't just feel wrong, it triggers the nervous system. When truth is a 10, anything less is somatic. You can feel the lie before it forms a word. If you lie, you knock your own nervous system off balance.
rigid judgment, self-righteousness, justice as control.
disruption of rigid patterns, revealing what's hidden through inversion, innovation through disorder. Sees the absurdity in what everyone else treats as fixed.
deception as lifestyle, instability mistaken for freedom.
alignment with biological truth, growth through patience rather than force. Thinks in cycles rather than straight lines.
rejection of structure, naturalism as escape from complexity.
navigation of the unseen, death and rebirth as structural realities. Can hold darkness without being consumed. Always drawn to what's hidden.
obsession with shadow, nihilism, identity built on the margin.
right action regardless of personal cost. Loyalty to what's true, not what's comfortable. Does the right thing even when no one is watching.
rigidity, losing self in obligation, duty performed for an audience.
the generative state of pure engagement. Awe. Creativity for its own sake. Not the absence of seriousness, the intelligence serious people miss. Always able to find what's alive in something.
avoidance through play, irresponsibility, lightness that refuses depth.
completion. Endings held cleanly. The threshold kept, the thread cut when the thread is finished, presence with what's dying without flinching. Releases what's done so renewal has room.
morbidity, clinging that refuses every ending, or dealing endings as power.
reads the pattern and its timing. Knows what must unfold and when to move. Acts at the right moment without forcing the thread.
fatalism, abdication of choice, reading the pattern as an excuse to never act.
the watch kept. A perimeter held so what's inside can live. Protection without possession, sanctuary without walls that strangle.
overprotection that smothers, vigilance that never rests, walls against life itself.
the one who makes sure there's enough, and not only for today. Supply held against a season nobody can see yet. The granary, the harvest, the wage. Provides for, rather than trades with.
worth measured only in what's furnished, hoarding dressed as prudence, the provider who can't be provided for.
One exact place in your body where a pattern sits. Every pattern has one. Release works at that place in the body, not on your thoughts.

The wear on your body from stress that keeps switching on and never fully switches off. It builds up like interest on a debt nobody paid. Release brings it down by working on the addresses where that stress is held.

One of 12 kinds of character you are born with. It is the third step down on the side of you that was there before life taught you anything: domains feed your blueprint, and your blueprint splits into archetypes. It is its own step, not another name for the blueprint. Because it was there first, it is not stored in the body and it is not released. The work changes where it points, not what it is.

When the world around you, and your own feelings, stop steering you. Things lose their grip because your survival patterns have stopped giving the orders. It is a way of running, not a finish line, so no number of releases counts you in.
Where you point your mind. It comes two ways: wide, taking everything in, or narrow, fixed on one thing. Attention steers. Will pushes.

A field around the body, said to come from the state of your nerves. This instrument does not measure it, and no instrument this product knows of does. Living tissue does give off very faint light. That light is real and comes from the cells' normal chemistry, but nobody has shown it carries the state of your nerves. The aura is kept here as a way to talk about how other people feel you, not as a reading.
How far open the soul's window is. The wider it opens, the more of what is really there you take in.

Very faint light given off by living tissue, too faint for your eyes to see. It is real, and labs have measured it since the 1950s. It comes from the cells' normal chemistry, not from the state of your nerves. This product does not claim it carries the aura, and nothing in the instrument reads it.

A seat. In this model, a field you cannot touch, made by a bundle of nerves. There are seven, from the base of the spine to the top of the head. Seven, with one nerve bundle each, is a modern Western idea: older traditions count five, six, eight or more, and matching seats to nerve bundles dates from 1927. The word is kept because the work is done in it, not because anyone has measured a chakra.
Survival energy stuck at one place in the body. It gets stuck when a stress reaction starts and never gets to finish. When your attention reaches it, it feels like heat, pressure, tingling or weight.

A sense beyond the five: seeing, hearing, feeling or knowing something without eyes, ears, skin or working it out. The names are clairvoyance, clairaudience, clairsentience and claircognizance, and there are others. Soma breaks them apart. Clear the soma and they work together.

When what you mean, what you do and what your body does all point the same way, with fewer parts of you pulling against each other. The instrument works it out from your answers. It does not measure your body. CQ is its number.

The quality a pattern was blocking, installed at the same address once the charge there is released. Where fear was held, trust. It shows up in what you do, what you feel and what your body does. It is not a general good feeling. It is the one quality this pattern kept out.

Energy that carries information, and you meet it two ways. At its widest it has no edges and no focus: infinite consciousness. At its narrowest it is you, aware, in one place. The same thing, seen through a wide opening or a small one.

Coherence Quotient, your coherence number. You answer questions on the 21 Laws of Moral Integrity, each scored 0 to 10, and CQ adds them up, out of 210. Nothing else goes into it. It starts at 0 and fills as you answer. The shadow never pulls it down. The shadow pulls on how you come across instead.

What happens to what you mean when it passes through places in the body that carry charge. The message leaves whole and comes out bent, like a straight stick that looks bent in water. It is a word for that bending and not a separate number: it used to be the same reading as SQ under a second name.

Decoherence, the shadow number. All the weight held at all 112 addresses, added up, against the most they could hold. A high DQ reads as energy spent holding up parts of you that pull against each other.

Everything slowing your willpower down, added together. Fetters, clenched muscles, inflammation and addresses carrying charge all pull on the link between your mind, body and spirit, like a heavy bag you have to haul. Drag is why willpower runs out.
A point just outside the body, at the centre between your feet. It holds you to the ground the way an anchor holds a boat.

The mind stuck to the body. It is never quite here: it flips between thinking and feeling to get through the day, and fear does the steering. The ego is the mask your character wears. It is your DQ, every SQ that is running, and every pattern and every kind of awareness that comes with living as a body, all added up.

A named pattern that sits at one address and fires when something matches it. There is one at every address, 112 in all: the ones in the body, plus four just outside it, two above the head and two below the feet. It fires when the match arrives, however long ago it was put there.

Five ways into the work, each named for a teacher. Krishna, flow. Buddha, awareness. Christ, the body. Rama, alignment. Lao Tzu, the horizontal. All five end at the same Source, and the Anchor Principle runs under all of them.

The part of what life taught you that does not wear off with time, with a big change in your life, or with most kinds of therapy. Only release at the address clears it. Habits you keep going by repeating them are different: a change in your life can clear those on its own.
A named group of saboteurs that run together as one. Heavier than a single saboteur, because each pattern in the group keeps the others going.

All of your coherence, added up. It lifts your nervous system by keeping you inside your own moral lines. Integrity is a ship's hull. A hole in the hull lets the water in. It has to be whole, a hundred percent, for the hull to hold, and for CQ to hold. It is measured by how closely you keep the 21 Laws of Moral Integrity.
What you mean to happen. It is part willpower, part wanting, part drive. Moving toward something feels good. If you have not picked what you want, avoiding things takes its place.

The way the body protects its own patterns. Blaming, changing the subject and making excuses are a tag fighting back, the way your body fights a germ. The body guards the pattern because the truth feels too hard to face. Narcissism is this, turned all the way up.

What your thoughts and actions send out into the world, and what comes back to you because of them. It goes round, like an echo. It comes back so you can learn the lesson, get past it, and send it on so it never comes back again. Karma is cause and effect, bouncing between you and the world.

One of six layers that everything you live through passes through, like light through six panes of coloured glass. The six are the body, energy, the mind, wisdom, bliss and language. Each one changes what passes through it.
Life energy stored at the base of the spine. It rises from there to the top of the head once enough addresses along the way are cleared, the way water runs once a pipe is unblocked.

The release protocol. It does two things, in order. First it lowers the charge at an address. Then, while that place is still open, it installs the quality the pattern was blocking. An affirmation does only the second and skips the first.

A tag that squeezes something big you lived through into a small label. Every time you say I am this, you make one. That is how labels work, not a judgment on you. The label is always smaller than what happened.

Built up distortion that has started to pass for who you are. It is what most people call their personality: patterns stored at addresses in the body, firing the way life trained them to. The mask is not who you are.
What is left when a vritti is taken as yours: what came in through your senses and your feelings, named as yours and stored in the body.

A spinning shape made of energy, used in the release protocol. Its top half spins left and its bottom half spins right. Spinning against each other, they shake up the flow at an address, and that opens it for release.

Another word for an address: one exact place on the body's energy map. There are 112. Most are in the body. Four sit just outside it: the Earth Star, centred between your feet, the Gaia Gateway below it, the Sol Star just above your head, and the Stellar Gateway above that.

A Sanskrit word meaning vigour. Life energy that builds up in meditation and wraps around you like a cocoon. The field of energy your nervous system gives off, set by the state it is in. As soma builds up it becomes load, like weight in a backpack. Where soma fields overlap they break up what you can perceive and make walls your awareness cannot see through.

The moment something that hit you hard gets a name and gets stored at an address. The name locks it in. From then on the body watches for anything that matches, and when it finds one, the pattern stored there fires.

The two steps a full release needs, in this order. First, Release: the charge at the address goes down. Second, Embodied Truth: while the address is open, the quality the pattern was blocking is installed. Do the first without the second and the address is left with nothing to run instead.

A ripple of what you sense and what you feel, coming in from outside. It travels along your nerves to your brain, where it is put together and noticed. Once you take it as yours, the vritti is what caves in the nerve, the chakra and your field of awareness.

It has no reading of its own: will is intention with a direction, and anything dragging on it shows up as resistance, which is already read.

A kink becomes a cluster. A cluster becomes a network.
Your body is expressive by default. Movement, breath, voice, appetite. Nothing held.
Stress makes it contract. That part is ordinary and the contraction is supposed to pass.
You identify with the contraction. A bias forms in the mind, and a kink of resistance forms in the shape of that stress response.
The response gets conditioned. Practised often enough that it fires without the event that taught it.
The node turns into a cluster. Three or four addresses now contract together as one structure.
Clusters form networks. The body tenses in different locations at once, because the structures are wired to each other.
Now the problem begins. You procrastinate more, feel anxious more, more shy, more depressed, more overwhelmed. The nervous system has kinks all over it, blocking the natural energy flow of the body.
The instrument finds the point of origin. It integrates the kink, the cluster and the network, in that order, starting where the sequence started.

The engine builds the reading in exactly those steps. A kink is one address carrying charge, and 4 or over counts as loaded. A cluster is three or four addresses tightening together, at an average of 3.7. A network joins two clusters from the same family, one of six, and then stacks those pairs. The clusters in one family sit in different parts of the body, so the network is the first step that shows up in more than one place.
